title: Introduction to Chemistry - Chemistry - Scope and Applications
subject: Chemistry

questions.q: Chemistry is best defined as the study of __________.
options: matter, its composition, properties, and the changes it undergoes
the motion of objects and the forces acting upon them
rocks, minerals, and the physical history of the earth
questions.explain: Chemistry is the science that deals with the materials of the universe (matter) and the changes that these materials undergo. (Source: OpenStax Chemistry 2e, Ch 1.1)
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: Which of the following represents a **macroscopic** observation?
options: A water molecule consists of two hydrogen atoms and one oxygen atom.
Iron rusts when exposed to moist air, turning reddish-brown.
The distance between carbon atoms in diamond is 154 pm.
Electrons orbit the nucleus in specific energy levels.
questions.explain: Macroscopic observations are those visible to the naked eye, such as the color change of rusting iron. The other options describe the microscopic (molecular/atomic) domain.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: Chemistry is often referred to as the "Central Science" because __________.
options: it is the only science that uses mathematics
it connects and overlaps with other sciences like biology, physics, and geology
it was the first science ever discovered
it deals exclusively with the center of the atom
questions.explain: Chemistry is central because the principles of matter and energy are fundamental to understanding biology, physics, geology, ecology, and many other disciplines.
